@graph.name: Ports & Intermodal Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The master dataset of the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the eight ports the company's crews serve with logistics project management, specialized labor, ocean container packing and unpacking, loading and unloading, cross-docking, transloading, 3PL support and freight rework — the Virginia Inland Port at Front Royal, the Port of Virginia at Norfolk (Norfolk International Terminals, Virginia International Gateway, Portsmouth Marine Terminal and Newport News Marine Terminal), Richmond Marine Terminal, the Port of Baltimore, the Port of Wilmington, Delaware, PhilaPort at Philadelphia, the Port of Huntington Tri-State river district, and the Port of New York and New Jersey. Each port is a full entity: authority and operator of record, terminal facts with acreage, berths, depth and capacity where the port authority publishes them, cargo specialties, rail service with on-dock and interchange qualifiers, highway corridors, foreign-trade-zone facts where designated, labeled volume figures with their sources and periods, current status items, and the branch binding that assigns the port to Winchester, VA or Martinsburg, WV by verified road distance. Portsmouth Marine Terminal is recorded as what it is — a heavy-lift and offshore-wind hub, not a container terminal; Virginia International Gateway is recorded as leased, not port-authority-owned; the Port of Wilmington's operator of record is Enstructure. No volume figure is published for the Virginia Inland Port, Richmond Marine Terminal or the Port of Wilmington, because none is verified. The company's crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards. The offer set does not include drayage: the company does not run port drayage — freight moves on the customer's or carrier's trucks, and the company's crews do the hands-on work at port-adjacent warehouses, receivers' docks, yards, leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes. Every fact carries its source; the companion coverage-matrix node in this file maps all 64 port-by-service cells.

Every cell binds to its port's branch: Winchester, VA for the Virginia Inland Port, the Port of Virginia, Richmond Marine Terminal and the Port of Huntington Tri-State (added 2026-11-07, WV-2 — an inland river port district bound on miles, 312.8 mi); Martinsburg, WV for Baltimore, Wilmington and PhilaPort (PhilaPort on drive time — road miles are tied) and the Port of New York and New Jersey (added 2026-11-10, Port #8 — bound on miles, 251.1 mi).

@graph.name: Virginia Inland Port
@graph.description: Virginia Inland Port (Front Royal, VA) — inland intermodal terminal (dry port). Authority: Virginia Port Authority. Operator: Virginia Port Authority. Cargo: intermodal containers moving between rail and truck under steamship bill of lading; on-site log stuffing. Rail: Norfolk Southern — on-terminal intermodal rail; the terminal sits adjacent to the NS Crescent Corridor main line; rail is the long-haul leg to and from the Norfolk Harbor terminals (NIT, VIG), truck is the last-mile leg. Highway corridors: I-81, I-66. Foreign-trade zone: FTZ 20, Site 7 — Warren County Industrial Corridor (490 acres, Routes 340/522/661) (grantee Virginia Port Authority). U.S. Customs port of entry. Branch binding: this port is served from the Winchester, VA branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 23 road miles from Winchester and 43 from Martinsburg; bound to Winchester on miles. about 20 mi / about 20 min closer from Winchester.

@graph.description: Port of Huntington Tri-State (Huntington, WV) — inland river port district (barge, bulk, breakbulk) — a U.S. Port Statistical Area spanning the Ohio, Kanawha and Big Sandy rivers in West Virginia, Ohio and Kentucky. Authority: Huntington District Waterways Association (the district is a Port Statistical Area, not a single port authority). Operator: Multiple private terminal and dock operators across the district (no single operator). Cargo: coal and lignite; gasoline, distillate fuel oil and petroleum products; chemicals; limestone and aggregates; steel-related cargo; crude materials. Rail: Norfolk Southern — serves the Ohio-side docks; mainline on the WV shore of the Big Sandy; CSX — serves the district; mainline on the KY shore of the Big Sandy. Highway corridors: US-52, I-64, US-23, US-60, US-32. Volume (CY2023, calendar): 29,699,657 short tons — Port Statistical Area basis — the district moves tens of millions of tons annually on every published basis; this is the USACE figure on the PSA basis (source: USACE Top-50 ports list (2023), via WV program research verification 2026-11-07). Branch binding: this port is served from the Winchester, VA branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 312.8 road miles from Winchester and 359 from Martinsburg; bound to Winchester on miles. about 45 mi closer from Winchester (measured range 357.7-360.4 mi from Martinsburg).

@graph.description: Port of New York and New Jersey (Elizabeth, NJ) — deepwater marine port (containers, autos and RoRo, bulk, breakbulk) — the largest container port on the U.S. East Coast and the third-largest in the United States. Authority: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. Operator: Multiple private terminal operators running Port Authority terminals under long-term leases (landlord port — the Port Authority owns the terminals, the operators run them). Cargo: containers; autos and roll-on/roll-off vehicles; bulk (salt, cement, edible oils and juice, aggregates); breakbulk and project cargo. Rail: CSX — Class I partner serving the port through the ExpressRail system; Norfolk Southern — Class I partner serving the port through the ExpressRail system; Conrail Shared Assets Operations — switching carrier for CSX and Norfolk Southern in the North Jersey shared-assets district — not a third Class I. Highway corridors: I-95 (New Jersey Turnpike), I-78, I-287, US-1/9. Foreign-trade zone: FTZ 49, Newark/Elizabeth (grantee The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey). U.S. Customs port of entry. Volume (CY2025, calendar): 8,897,531 TEU — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ year-end 2025 release, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 8,698,526 TEU — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Cargo Facility Charge Annual Report 2025, Table 2, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 410,092 autos (units) — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Port 2024 At A Glance, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10).
